notes: Inputs: idea.md, market_insights (apps + web-search, 2026-11), memory/extra-context/core-human-desires.md (framework). user_extraction.json does NOT exist — identity driver not extracted; proceeded without it. SCORING LOGIC: The underlying GOAL (a sarkari naukri) is one of the strongest desires in Indian society — livelihood security (survival: ~80% of Indian job aspirants still pursue govt jobs per CMIE via Business Today; RRB NTPC 2025 ~1.22 crore applicants for ~11.6K posts) and family/marriage-market status. But the app does not deliver the goal; it delivers 'feeling in control / not missing out' around the goal. Control = 4: fear of missing a deadline is real (news reports of aspirants unable to apply near deadlines; Careers360: many miss opportunities because unaware of last dates) and FOMO drives aspirants to join 5-10 Telegram channels. Survival = 4: a missed form can cost a year in a multi-year (3-6 yr) prep cycle, and age-limit cut-offs make some misses permanent. Status = 3: the job is status-laden, the reminder app is not; streaks/progress add only a little. Belonging = 2: prep is socially embedded (Telegram groups, YouTube communities) but an alert app is solitary. Curiosity = 1. Weighted strength = (survival 4 x0.3 + control 4 x0.3 + status 3 x0.2 + belonging 2 x0.1 + curiosity 1 x0.1) = 3.3 -> 'moderate'. Label is deliberately NOT 'strong': desire for the OUTCOME is strong, desire for THIS PRODUCT is moderate because free substitutes (Telegram, Testbook/Adda247 alerts, Google) already satisfy most of the control need — the app only removes residual anxiety (noise, eligibility doubt). At least one dimension >= 3, so no weak-desire flag. VIRALITY medium: aspirants intensely forward notifications in WhatsApp/Telegram groups, but they forward the official PDF/link, not an app; a shareable 'exams you are eligible for' card could ride this, unvalidated.
